scenes.heading: Order of operations with integers
scenes.say: Is negative five plus three times negative four equal to eight, or negative seventeen? Only one answer is right. Let's see why order matters.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.science: Brackets and powers come before × ÷, then + −
scenes.breaks: You can choose to put your shirt or pants on first, but in maths the order is fixed.
scenes.say: Think about getting dressed. Socks go on before shoes. Do it the other way and you get a strange result. Calculations are the same. There's an agreed order, and brackets are like a note saying do this bit first.

scenes.heading: BIDMAS
steps: Division and Multiplication, left to right
Addition and Subtraction, left to right
scenes.say: The order is BIDMAS. Brackets first. Then indices, which are powers. Then division and multiplication, left to right. Then addition and subtraction, left to right.

scenes.heading: Multiply first
scenes.question: Work out −5 + 3 × (−4).
scenes.say: Work out negative five plus three times negative four. Multiply first: three times negative four is negative twelve. Then negative five plus negative twelve is negative seventeen.
scenes.caption: Work out −5 + 3 × (−4). Multiply first: 3 × (−4) = −12. Then −5 + (−12) = −17.

scenes.heading: Watch the brackets
scenes.say: Watch the brackets with powers. Negative three, in brackets, squared means negative three times negative three, which is nine. But without brackets, only the three is squared, so it's negative nine.
scenes.caption: Watch the brackets with powers. (−3)² means (−3) × (−3), which is 9. But without brackets, only the 3 is squared, so −3² is −9.

scenes.heading: Powers first
scenes.question: Work out 2 × (−3)² − 10.
scenes.say: Work out two times negative three squared, minus ten. Indices first: negative three squared is nine. Then two times nine is eighteen. Eighteen minus ten is eight.
scenes.caption: Work out 2 × (−3)² − 10. Indices first: (−3)² = 9. Then 2 × 9 = 18. 18 − 10 = 8.

scenes.heading: Tips to remember
points: Do one step, rewrite the whole line
A fraction bar is a big bracket
Predict the sign before you finish
scenes.say: Some tips. Do one step, then rewrite the whole line, so no signs go missing. Bracket it to square it is a made-up trick for negative powers. And a fraction bar works like brackets on the top and the bottom.

points: Use the integer sign rules at each step
scenes.say: Quick recap. Follow BIDMAS every time, and use the integer sign rules at each step. Negative three in brackets squared is nine, but without brackets it's negative nine. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Follow BIDMAS every time, and use the integer sign rules at each step. (−3)² = 9, but −3² = −9. Now try the practice questions!
